facts.fact: Cache-Control: max-age=31536000 caches a response for one year, the usual setting for versioned files.
ETag carries a server-chosen token, often a hash of the content, that the client sends back in If-None-Match.
A 304 Not Modified response carries no body, so revalidation transfers very little.
no-cache allows storing but forces revalidation before reuse; no-store forbids storing.
Without Cache-Control, responses are still cached heuristically.
The specification suggests reusing a heuristically cached response for about 10% of the time since it was last modified.
Expires was HTTP/1.0's freshness header; when both are present, max-age wins.
Vary keys stored responses by request headers such as Accept-Language.
A private cache belongs to one client; a shared cache sits between client and server and serves many users.
The immutable directive stops revalidation on reload for content that never changes.
QPACK predefines one-week, one-month and one-year max-age values that compress to one byte in HTTP/3.
Clear-Site-Data: cache clears browser caches but has no effect on intermediate caches.
ETag is recommended over Last-Modified because it is more accurate.
Build tools such as webpack can add hash fingerprints to asset URLs automatically.
private, max-age=600 lets the browser, but not intermediary caches, keep a response for 10 minutes.

plan.problem: The page's canonical is https://web.dev/articles/http-cache, and in this run a plain fetch of that URL (no Accept-Language) was redirected to the French ?hl=fr version. A crawler that follows the canonical may store the page in a language the reader did not ask for.
plan.fix: Serve the canonical URL in its default language to clients that send no Accept-Language, and keep the language variants on hreflang alternates.

plan.problem: Under "Common caching patterns" an h3 reads "Validation", the same text as the earlier h2. The chunker matches heading lines by text, so #22 to #24 are filed under the wrong section and "Validation" ends up holding 31% of the page.

plan.before: Don't forget to set the Last-Modified and ETag headers, so that you don't have to re-transmit a resource when reloading.
plan.after: For cache-busted static files, also set Last-Modified and ETag, so that a reload revalidates the file instead of re-transmitting it.

plan.problem: "Types of caches" runs to about 5,000 characters under one h2, so the window cuts it and #3 opens with "proxy-revalidate However".

plan.before: proxy-revalidate However, in recent years, as HTTPS has become more common and client/server communication has become encrypted, proxy caches in the path can only tunnel a response and can't behave as a cache, in many cases.
plan.after: Proxy caches and HTTPS: now that most traffic is encrypted, a proxy cache on the path can usually only tunnel the response and cannot cache it.
